Mispricing hypothesis

p = 0.307 in the refined out-of-sample test.

The founding hypothesis failed, and that shaped this interface.

Players flagged by the residual showed no supported subsequent appreciation advantage. They exited top-five football at 3.7 times the benchmark rate, 30.1% versus 8.2%.

What it does

Estimates what a player's market value would be if it followed observable performance, age, position, league and career trajectory. It then compares that estimate to market value and separately estimates exit risk.

What it does not do

It does not establish that a valuation gap is exploitable mispricing. No player is labelled “undervalued”. The language is “potential valuation discrepancy — investigate”.

What the model does not know

Contract length and expiry, injury history and current fitness, scouting and tactical assessment, off-field circumstances, agent/release-clause situation, and willingness to move are outside the public information set.

Decision rule: ask why the player is cheap, and whether the model knows enough to call the discrepancy an opportunity.
